chief_complaint: acute auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, and disorganized behavior over 2 months
hpi_details: 24M college student brought by campus security after barricading himself in his dorm room for 5 days. Claims the FBI has implanted a microchip in his dental filling to broadcast his thoughts and monitor his actions. Reports hearing two distinct voices commanding him to smash his computer. Has stopped attending classes, neglected personal hygiene, and shows flat affect with formal thought disorder (derailment).
ideas: believes the hospital is part of a government surveillance network
concerns: terrified the voices will punish him if he cooperates with medical staff
expectations: wants his phone back immediately so he can expose the conspiracy online
pmh: No prior psychiatric history; cannabis use socially

investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent first-episode psychosis results are now available; safety observation and psychiatric admission should not be delayed.

results.value: Positive for cannabinoids; negative for amphetamines and cocaine

clinical_knowledge.topic: First-Episode Psychosis / Schizophrenia evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of First-Episode Psychosis / Schizophrenia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes urgent psychiatric admission for safety and diagnostic evaluation, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: acute auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, and disorganized behavior over 2 months

Key HPI features: 24M college student brought by campus security after barricading himself in his dorm room for 5 days. Claims the FBI has implanted a microchip in his dental filling to broadcast his thoughts and monitor his actions. Reports hearing two distinct voices commanding him to smash his computer. Has stopped attending classes, neglected personal hygiene, and shows flat affect with formal thought disorder (derailment).

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 88, BP 124/80. Patient is unkempt, malodorous, with suspicious guarded posture and poor eye contact. Speech is fluent but exhibits loose associations and tangentiality. Affect is blunted and incongruent. Endorses third-person commanding auditory hallucinations and thought broadcasting. Cognitive orientation intact. Urine drug screen negative for amphetamines/cocaine, positive for cannabinoids. Comprehensive lab workup (TSH, RPR, B12, CMP) and head CT unremarkable, ruling out organic secondary causes.
Relevant background/PMH: No prior psychiatric history; cannabis use socially
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out First-Episode Psychosis / Schizophrenia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bipolar I with psychotic features without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Command auditory hallucinations.
management_principles: Urgently admit to an acute psychiatric inpatient unit; maintain observation and assess risk to self or others, including whether command hallucinations are actionable
After psychiatric assessment, consider a second-generation antipsychotic with baseline and ongoing metabolic, neurologic, and other indicated monitoring
Provide low-stimulus environment and supportive reality-oriented nursing care
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 24M first-episode presentation of psychosis characterized by persecutory/passivity delusions, third-person auditory hallucinations, and negative symptoms lasting >1 month.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 88, BP 124/80. Patient is unkempt, malodorous, with suspicious guarded posture and poor eye contact. Speech is fluent but exhibits loose associations and tangentiality. Affect is blunted and incongruent. Endorses third-person commanding auditory hallucinations and thought broadcasting. Cognitive orientation intact. Urine drug screen negative for amphetamines/cocaine, positive for cannabinoids. Comprehensive lab workup (TSH, RPR, B12, CMP) and head CT unremarkable, ruling out organic secondary causes.
reference_soap.assessment: First-Episode Psychosis, schizophreniform disorder vs Schizophrenia (meeting DSM-5 Criterion A symptoms with duration >1 month and marked functional impairment).
reference_soap.plan: Urgently admit to an acute psychiatric inpatient unit for safety and diagnostic evaluation, with observation and assessment of risk to self or others, including whether command hallucinations are actionable. After psychiatric assessment, consider a second-generation antipsychotic with baseline and ongoing metabolic, neurologic, and other indicated monitoring. Provide a low-stimulus environment and supportive reality-oriented nursing care. Obtain collateral and capacity assessment as clinically indicated; involve social work for family psychoeducation and referral to an early-intervention psychosis program.

learning_objectives: Perform a structured mental status examination assessing for formal thought disorder, delusions, and perceptual disturbances
Differentiate primary psychotic disorders (Schizophrenia/Schizophreniform) from substance-induced psychosis and organic medical conditions
Select first-line second-generation antipsychotic pharmacotherapy and monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) and metabolic side effects
Outline principles of early intervention and family psychoeducation in first-episode psychosis

teaching.one_liner: Psychotic disorder characterized by delusions, auditory hallucinations, disorganized thought processes, and negative symptoms.
red_flags: Severe paranoia with threat to self/others
Suicidal thoughts, intent, plan, or access to means
Violent thoughts, intent, or inability to resist harmful commands

must_ask.say: Do you hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
Do you feel that people are watching, spying, or trying to harm you?
Do you ever feel like your mind is being broadcasted aloud or controlled by outside forces?
Have you been using cannabis, amphetamines, or hallucinogens recently?
Have you isolated yourself from friends or stopped attending work or school?
Have the voices told you to hurt yourself or anyone else, and do you feel you might act on that?
